title: Prima la farmacia
summary: Italy's pharmacy-first health culture, the mal di… formula, and booking a doctor's appointment

blocks.title: Prima la farmacia
blocks.body: For a headache, a cough, a small cut — Italians go to **la farmacia** before a doctor. Look for the green cross (**la croce verde**), often blinking; a *farmacista* can look at your symptoms, sell you something, and tell you if you actually need a doctor. When the local farmacia is closed, one nearby stays open on rotation — **la farmacia di turno**, posted on the door.
blocks.callout: Farmacia first, medico second — that's the everyday order in Italy.

blocks.title: Mal di…
blocks.body: For aches and pains, Italian uses the fixed pattern **mal di + body part** — no article: *mal di testa* (headache), *mal di gola* (sore throat), *mal di pancia* (stomach ache), *mal di denti* (toothache), *mal di schiena* (backache). Pair it with *avere*: *ho mal di testa*.
blocks.callout: No il/la after mal di — it's a fixed little formula, learn it as one chunk.

blocks.prompt: You have a mild headache. What's the everyday first move in Italy?
options: Vai in farmacia e chiedi consiglio al farmacista
blocks.explain: For something small, the farmacista is the normal first stop — fast, no appointment, and they'll tell you if you need more.

blocks.hint: mal di + body part, no article, with avere.
blocks.explain: *Ho mal di gola* — the fixed formula, no il/la needed.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.

blocks.scene: 'You' mention feeling unwell to Giulia, who explains the farmacia-first habit and when to actually see a doctor

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ho mal di testa e un po' di mal di gola.
lines.en: I have a headache and a bit of a sore throat.

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.nl: Allora vai in farmacia, qui all'angolo — il farmacista ti consiglia qualcosa subito.
lines.en: Then go to the pharmacy, right on the corner — the pharmacist will recommend something right away.
lines.spotlight: Giulia's first move is the farmacia, not the doctor — that's the everyday Italian order.

lines.speaker: You
lines.en: And if it doesn't go away?

lines.speaker: Giulia
lines.nl: Se tra due o tre giorni stai ancora male, prendi un appuntamento dal dottore.
lines.en: If in two or three days you still feel unwell, book an appointment with the doctor.
